newsitem.title: FRANCE: Douwe Egberts France raises retail coffee prices.
newsitem.headline: Douwe Egberts France raises retail coffee prices.

text.p: Douwe Egberts France said on Friday it had raised retail prices by 1.50 francs per 250 grams of arabica coffee and by 65 centimes for each pack of robusta coffee, with immediate effect.
This brings total price hikes for the group to 45-47 percent for arabicas and to around 15 percent for robustas since the beginning of the year, chairman Pascal Jouannet told Reuters.
Douwe Egberts France, the French unit of Dutch coffee roaster Douwe Egberts, controls 15 percent of the domestic coffee market.
Douwe Egberts is owned by Sara Lee Corp.
Jouannet said the move was aimed at keeping up with soaring world futures in the face of tight supplies in Latin America and low stocks in consumer countries.
"Stocks are very very tight", he said, adding that on some origins, notably washed arabicas, roasters were operating on a cargo by cargo basis.
Jouannet also said that he expected prices to remain volatile until at least the autumn as Brazil's frost season was fast approaching.

"All supplies are in the hands of origin countries. We are now entering the period when everyone is watching for possible frost in Brazil. Things may cool down in the autumn but that is not certain," he said.

On Thursday coffee futures hit their highest levels in 20 years. New York futures reached a high of 279.00 cents a pound, the highest price for a coffee futures contract on the exchange since June 1977.
